title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #10

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which tool is good for smudging charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. A finger or a tissue
   B. A knife
   C. A stone
   D. A wet brush of paint

2. Macramé is a technique of (1 mark)
   A. carving wood
   B. beating drums
   C. painting on cloth
   D. tying knots to make patterns and shapes

3. In netball, the ball is moved mainly by (1 mark)
   A. passing it
   B. rolling it
   C. kicking it
   D. running with it

4. Red mixed with yellow makes (1 mark)
   A. orange
   B. green
   C. purple
   D. brown

5. On the colour wheel, green sits between (1 mark)
   A. red and yellow
   B. red and blue
   C. yellow and blue
   D. orange and purple

6. A flat brush is best for (1 mark)
   A. cutting paper
   B. wide areas
   C. writing with ink
   D. tiny details only

7. The French rhythm name for a pair of quavers is (1 mark)
   A. taa
   B. rest
   C. ta-te
   D. tee-taa

8. How many notes are in the melody d r m m r d? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Five
   C. Six
   D. Four

9. A well known children's song that uses only m r d is (1 mark)
   A. A drum solo
   B. Hot Cross Buns
   C. A song with many notes
   D. The national anthem

10. How many rectangular slabs of different sizes are cut in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. One
   C. Ten
   D. Three

11. What is clay? (1 mark)
   A. A metal
   B. Fine sticky soil that is soft when wet and hard when dry
   C. A kind of wood
   D. A type of paper

12. The Kodaly hand sign for d is (1 mark)
   A. a closed fist
   B. a pointing finger
   C. a sloping palm
   D. a flat hand held level

13. Why do we knead clay before using it? (1 mark)
   A. To make it smooth and remove air
   B. To make it dry
   C. To make it black
   D. To make it hard

14. What is the first command at the start of a race? (1 mark)
   A. Stop
   B. Set
   C. Go
   D. On your marks

15. A sprint is (1 mark)
   A. a short race run at full speed
   B. a very long race
   C. a jump into sand
   D. a throwing event

16. The Kenyan flag has stripes of (1 mark)
   A. red, white and blue
   B. black, red and green with thin white stripes
   C. orange and green
   D. blue, yellow and white

17. Which is a safe surface for gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. A stony floor
   B. A mat or soft clean ground
   C. Wet tiles
   D. Concrete

18. At the start of the side roll, your arms are (1 mark)
   A. behind your back
   B. on your knees
   C. stretched above your head
   D. folded on your chest

19. Gestures in singing are (1 mark)
   A. words only
   B. quiet time
   C. hand and body movements that fit the song
   D. sounds of the drum

20. Which folk songs are sung while working? (1 mark)
   A. Funeral songs
   B. Naming songs
   C. Work songs
   D. Marriage songs

21. The battery of a camera (1 mark)
   A. gives it power
   B. cleans the lens
   C. keeps it dry
   D. takes the photo

22. Early morning and late afternoon light is (1 mark)
   A. absent
   B. harsh
   C. too dark always
   D. soft and gentle

23. Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1 and 2 covered? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. G
   C. D
   D. B

24. The song Hot Cross Buns can be played on (1 mark)
   A. only drums
   B. C D E only
   C. only G and C
   D. B A G

25. A squeaky, very high sound usually means you are (1 mark)
   A. playing a drum
   B. blowing too gently
   C. holding it upside down
   D. blowing too hard

26. Why should recorders not be shared without cleaning? (1 mark)
   A. Germs can spread through the mouthpiece
   B. They become heavy
   C. They change colour
   D. They melt

27. The top part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. head joint
   B. bell
   C. foot joint
   D. middle joint

28. How many finger holes are on the front of the descant recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. Twelve
   C. Three
   D. Seven

29. In a glide, your arms are (1 mark)
   A. stretched above the head with palms together
   B. folded
   C. by your sides
   D. behind your back

30. The elephant walk stretches the (1 mark)
   A. tongue
   B. ears
   C. nose
   D. back and the back of the legs

31. Before animal games you should (1 mark)
   A. sleep
   B. eat a big meal
   C. fight
   D. warm up

32. An elephant walk suits which rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   B. Very fast ta-te ta-te
   C. No beat
   D. A whistle

33. Why are indigenous games part of our heritage? (1 mark)
   A. They come to us from earlier generations
   B. They are foreign
   C. They have no meaning
   D. They were bought yesterday

34. Animal games are inspired by (1 mark)
   A. tall buildings
   B. cars
   C. the movements and behaviour of animals
   D. clouds

35. What should be written on the portfolio label? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. A secret
   C. Your name, class and title
   D. The price

36. How can you decorate a portfolio cover? (1 mark)
   A. By tearing it
   B. By burning it
   C. By putting sand on it
   D. By pasting coloured paper or fabric

37. Why should you write the date on each work in your portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. For fun only
   B. To spoil it
   C. To show when it was made
   D. To hide it

38. Which is an example of appropriate behaviour when viewing a display? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at others
   B. Being quiet and respectful
   C. Running
   D. Touching wet paint

39. How many verses does the Kenya National Anthem have? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. One
   C. Two
   D. Three

40. Aesthetic refers to (1 mark)
   A. how long it is
   B. how beautiful or pleasing something is
   C. how heavy it is
   D. how cheap it is

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how to make flour paste glue. (3 marks)

42. Give three examples of good etiquette during a performance. (3 marks)

43. How should we behave towards the national flag? (3 marks)

44. Describe the Kodaly hand sign for each of d, r and m. (3 marks)

45. Explain how working in pairs helps when learning the crab balance. (3 marks)

46. Identify the kayamba and the drum by giving the name, the community or area and the way of playing for each. (4 marks)

47. Describe the sit-and-slide water entry. (3 marks)

48. State four safety rules for the swimming pool. (4 marks)

49. Why should you collect only dead or fallen twigs for charcoal? (2 marks)

50. Describe how to paint a fruit so that it looks round using colour value. (4 marks)

51. Explain how to make a tint of blue. (2 marks)

52. Explain why a pair of quavers is the same length as one crotchet. (3 marks)

53. Why should we enter the water feet first? (2 marks)

54. Describe how to critique a friend's rhythmic pattern with respect. (4 marks)

55. State what the colours black and green stand for on the Kenyan flag. (2 marks)

56. Name any two players' positions in netball. (2 marks)

57. Describe how to make a ball using the macramé technique and overhand knots. (5 marks)

58. Explain how to write a rhythm from dictation. (3 marks)

59. State three ways of showing fair play in a netball game. (3 marks)

60. Why is swimming an essential life skill? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — A finger or a tissue
   A finger or tissue blends charcoal softly.

2. D — tying knots to make patterns and shapes
   Macramé is done by tying cords in knots.

3. A — passing it
   Players may not run with the ball, so they pass it to move it forward.

4. A — orange
   Red and yellow together give orange.

5. C — yellow and blue
   Green sits between the two primary colours that make it.

6. B — wide areas
   Flat brushes cover wide areas quickly.

7. C — ta-te
   Ta-te is two short sounds in one beat.

8. C — Six
   Count d, r, m, m, r, d to get six.

9. B — Hot Cross Buns
   Hot Cross Buns uses only three notes.

10. D — Three
   Three slabs are cut, one for each of d, r and m.

11. B — Fine sticky soil that is soft when wet and hard when dry
   Clay is a fine, sticky soil used for modelling.

12. A — a closed fist
   Doh is shown with a fist.

13. A — To make it smooth and remove air
   Kneading makes clay smooth and easy to shape.

14. D — On your marks
   The starter first says on your marks.

15. A — a short race run at full speed
   Sprints such as 50 m or 100 m are short races.

16. B — black, red and green with thin white stripes
   The flag has black, red, green and white.

17. B — A mat or soft clean ground
   Soft, flat surfaces prevent injuries.

18. C — stretched above your head
   Arms overhead with palms together keep the body long.

19. C — hand and body movements that fit the song
   Gestures help tell the story of a song.

20. C — Work songs
   Work songs give rhythm to work.

21. A — gives it power
   Without power the device will not work.

22. D — soft and gentle
   These times give soft light.

23. A — A
   A uses thumb, 1 and 2.

24. D — B A G
   It uses the three notes B, A and G.

25. D — blowing too hard
   Gentle air makes a good tone.

26. A — Germs can spread through the mouthpiece
   Saliva can carry disease-causing germs.

27. A — head joint
   The head joint has the mouthpiece.

28. D — Seven
   There are seven on the front and one thumb hole at the back.

29. A — stretched above the head with palms together
   Arms overhead create a streamlined shape.

30. D — back and the back of the legs
   Bending forward stretches those muscles.

31. D — warm up
   Warming up prepares muscles.

32. A — Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   Slow heavy steps.

33. A — They come to us from earlier generations
   Heritage is what we inherit.

34. C — the movements and behaviour of animals
   Children copy how animals move.

35. C — Your name, class and title
   A label shows whose portfolio it is.

36. D — By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   Decorating uses local resources.

37. C — To show when it was made
   Dates show how your skills grow.

38. B — Being quiet and respectful
   Respect for others' work is important.

39. D — Three
   The anthem has three verses.

40. B — how beautiful or pleasing something is
   Aesthetic is about beauty.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mix flour with a little cold water to a smooth paste. An adult adds hot water while stirring. Let it cool before use.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk on and off quietly, listen to the leader, do not talk or laugh, clap for others, bow at the end. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not let it touch the ground, do not write on it, keep it clean and not torn, and stand still and quiet when it is raised.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: d is a closed fist, r is a sloping palm, m is a flat palm held level.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: One learner performs while the other watches and checks, gives feedback, and helps if needed. They swap places.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kayamba: coastal people such as the Mijikenda, played by shaking. Drum (ngoma): found in many communities, played with hands or sticks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name, community or area and method, up to 4.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit on the edge with feet in the water, hands on the edge beside the hips. Turn to face the wall and slide gently into the water holding the edge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Swim only when watched; never swim alone; walk on the pool side; no pushing; no diving in shallow water; follow the whistle. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: To protect the environment and living trees. Dead twigs are also dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for protecting living trees, 1 mark for the environment or dry wood.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline. Paint the main colour. Add a lighter tone on the side facing the light and a darker tone on the side away from the light. Blend the edges and add a shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add white to blue, a little at a time, until it is as light as you want.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for white, 1 mark for adding gradually.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quaver is half a beat. Half plus half makes one whole beat. A crotchet is one beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is safer because you cannot hit your head on the bottom, and you can see where you land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Say one good thing first. Talk about the steadiness of the beat, variation and the ending. Give one suggestion to make it better. Listen to others' views politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Black stands for the people of Kenya. Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Goal Shooter, Goal Attack, Wing Attack, Centre, Wing Defence, Goal Defence, Goal Keeper. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a firm core from paper or cloth. Cut equal cords. Tie them together with an overhand knot at the middle. Put the core on top. Tie overhand knots between pairs of neighbouring cords to make a net around the core. Gather the cords at the bottom and tie a strong knot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear stages.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen twice to the pattern. Count the beats. For each beat decide if it was one long sound, two short sounds or silence, and write taa, ta-te or a rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Follow the rules; respect the umpire; shake hands with the other team; take turns in positions; encourage teammates. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps people stay safe near water and prevent drowning, and it keeps the body fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
